title: Observed Anomalies When Using Vertex Animation Texture (VAT) with MultiMeshInstance
body:
### Tested versions

v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono - Windows 11 (build 22621) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12400F (12 threads) - 23.81 GiB memory

### Issue description

To implement Vertex Animation Texture (VAT)  on a MultiMeshInstance node for efficient instanced crowd animation.

Reproducible anomalies occur when the source model contains two or more separate meshes. Single-mesh models function correctly.

1 Phenomenon A: Vertex Index Offset

Description: In the vertex shader, directly using the vertex_index from uv.x each vertex appears to sample data intended for the preceding vertex, causing overall animation misalignment.

Interim Workaround: Manually adjusting the sampling index to VERTEX_ID + 1 in the shader corrects the animation for most vertices. This suggests a consistent offset may be present in the vertex index mapping during data transfer.

2 Phenomenon B: Terminal Vertices Locked/Missing

Description: Even after applying the VERTEX_ID + 1 adjustment, the animation remains imperfect. Further investigation revealed:

The vertex with the highest VERTEX_ID value in the combined mesh remains completely static, frozen in its bind pose, and unresponsive to animation.

The vertex with the second-highest VERTEX_ID value appears to be non-existent in the render; its associated triangle faces are not drawn.

Additional Test: Suspecting potential out-of-bounds texture access, the EXR texture width was expanded to include unused "padding" pixels beyond the required vertex data area. This did not resolve the locked/missing vertex issue.
